findings.what: Z80 assembly uses toolchain.tool(), which checks only executable existence, without verified_binutils("z80-elf"); the full receipt verifies/records only m68k binutils. A private substituted assembler, explicitly rejected by the real pin checker, was nevertheless accepted by z80_sources and the full-image pipeline: it compiled the canonical bootstrap instead of a wrong registered source, yielding PASS and a receipt bound to the wrong source hash. No installed binary was modified. This reproduces a source-provenance failure under an unpinned/replaced Z80 tool.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify all executed Z80 binutils with the existing verified_binutils convention before use, bind those verified executable hashes into full-build receipts, and add a mismatched-Z80-executable negative regression.

findings.what: Duplicate Z80 target-unit registrations silently overwrite data["units"][k]. With real pinned tools, a 38-byte wrong NOP bootstrap registered before the correct bootstrap for InitialZ80Bootstrap is hidden by the later entry: the full-ROM build PASSes and records both source hashes, although the wrong assembled image demonstrably differs. The otherwise same build with only that wrong bootstrap FAILs at 0x0002c6. A wrong registered source can therefore pass by never contributing to the final image.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject duplicate Z80 target-unit registrations before assembly and require each accepted registration to remain a unique replacement in the final image. Add the wrong-then-correct duplicate-registration case as a regression.
